Create this independently assigned arm as a random, complex, photorealistic visual-semantics test of an original adult performer actively playing a physically recognizable alto saxophone, while using the attachment only for scoped visible appearance continuity.

Create a complex independent saxophone-semantics test photograph in a botanical research glasshouse at blue hour. An original adult saxophonist plays a sustained phrase while the automated misting system activates, with fine droplets catching diffuse blue skylight and narrow amber grow-lamp pools behind her. Show a vertical three-quarter, mid-to-knee view from a natural 50 mm perspective: her face and embouchure, both hands on the keywork, the curved neck and black mouthpiece, the long tapering lacquered-brass alto saxophone body, and its flared bell all remain legible at realistic scale. Her top teeth rest on the mouthpiece while her lower lip cushions the single cane reed; its tan edge and metal ligature are visible at the corner of her mouth. Her left hand supports the upper stack and her right hand works the lower stack. Dense rods, pads, key cups, and pearl touches run along the conical body. Image 1 is only a scoped visible-appearance reference for this original adult performer: long dark wavy hair with a center part, softly defined eyes, muted rose lips, and a luminous natural skin-surface finish. Preserve documentary skin and brass texture, crisp hand-to-key contact, condensation on the glass, and shallow but sufficient depth of field.
